title: A tree chooses a question, then asks again

blocks.text: The six-point dataset has class zero at both ends and class one in the middle. One threshold cannot isolate the middle interval on both sides, which makes recursion visible. The root scans candidate thresholds halfway between consecutive distinct feature values. For each candidate, it computes the impurity of both children, weighted by their sizes.
Build a binary CART classifier with exhaustive Gini splits. Return nested dictionaries: leaves contain prediction; internal nodes contain feature, threshold, left, right, and prediction.

A classification tree partitions feature space with threshold questions. Gini impurity is 1 minus the sum of squared class proportions. A pure node has impurity zero. A recursive algorithm applies the same split-search process independently to each child.

The best root threshold in this example is 1.5. It isolates two pure class-zero points on the left. The right child remains mixed and can ask another question. With depth two, that child splits at 3.5 and separates the middle class-one points from the last class-zero points. With depth one, recursion stops and the mixed child predicts its majority class instead.

blocks.text: The supplied score is a size-weighted sum rather than a weighted average. Because every candidate at one node has the same total number of rows, dividing by that total would not change the selected threshold. This equivalence applies within one node’s split search. It does not mean unweighted averages of child impurities are interchangeable.

Every node stores a prediction, including internal nodes. Leaves contain only a prediction, while internal nodes add feature, threshold, left, and right entries. Equality goes to the left branch through <=. Ties are resolved by the search order because the code updates the best split only for a strictly smaller score. The function does not impose a minimum impurity improvement, so it can split even without a positive gain. Preserve these details when comparing the returned dictionary with another implementation.

checks.prompt: A node contains only one class. What is its Gini impurity?

explanation.default: Revisit the stated quantities and units. Its class probability is 1, so 1−1²=0.

checks.prompt: A node has two equally frequent classes. What is its Gini impurity?

explanation.default: Revisit the stated quantities and units. 1−0.5²−0.5²=0.5.
